content.contents: hello :3
time to talk about my new album, 'GO UNTIL YOU ARE GONE'

in this blog post you'll find some BTS, some information on what the album (and imagery pertained thereto) means, and just general shit-shooting. i'm quite sick at the moment with a bad headcold so, hopefully this comes across somewhat coherent, but i'm loaded up on LEEEEANNNNN just kiddng i wouldn't haha i don't think cough syrup here in the UK has codeine anyway... i'm actually on paracetamol and white monster. goated combo. i can't fucking taste a thing.
so, let's talk! GUYAG! the first pressing question, and something i've kind of eluded to in previous blogs... what does GO UNTIL YOU ARE GONE actually mean?

well, i guess it's somewhat of a critique of capitalism. it's what we all do. we keep going until we are no more. that's what life has to be. once you start 'going' in school, the systems in place direct you to keep going. you don't have much of a choice in the matter. if you want to stop you'd better be prepared not to have any easy access to healthcare, food, water, the necessities of human survival. thus, there is no stopping, there is no rest, there is no choice. all one can do is go, until they are gone. that's how i've read it. and maybe as the artist who came up with the title i could sit here and say that's the definitive meaning but, i'd also very much encourage people to take their own meaning from it! make of my art what you will, that's what art is for!
i can still remember the exact moment the title came to me. here's a photo from it:

given, i'm doubtful this is the *exact* moment the phrase came to mind, but my beautiful girlfriend happened to be snapping pictures of me at the time it was bouncing around in there. this is on top of an old hill-fort or something, i don't know, i'm not a fucking nerd like that (sunglasses emoji). to me it's a mound, with some historical significance, which is cool! but my mind was obviously elsewhere. i just remember thinking how much i liked the phrase, GO UNTIL YOU ARE GONE in that moment. this photo was taken on or around February 3rd, so that's about when the title was decided. those keen-eyed of you may have noticed this photo is cropped to be square, like... an album cover. at the time i was writing a lot more acoustic guitar singer-songwriter music, which i've spoken a lot about in prior blogs, and i guess this was another potential cover i would've used for that album. i thought maybe i'd put the GO UNTIL YOU ARE GONE text in the top right corner. for that album, though, i've got another photo planned.

back in february was when i decided, too, that i wanted to start work on the next static.grl album. releasing “THE WIRED” had given me a small bout of confidence that was much needed after taking a long break from static.work in summer, 2024. it was around this time i reached out to chocoa.

chocoa was an artist i knew of for a short while. i think i started following his instagram around mid-to-late 2023, if not a bit earlier, after his art was randomly recommended thru the algorithm. i had messaged him a couple times, commented on a few works he'd posted, but it never went further than that. not until i saw another post from him in early 2025, and thought, actually, i think he could make a fantastic album cover. as such, i proposed the idea to him. he asked to hear some of my music, and as i recall he was particularly fond of statc.grl EP and THE WIRED. so it was agreed, he'd make the artwork for my next album. initially, i asked if he'd be interested in doing a few pieces of artwork, in case i did some kind of limited CD run or something, it would be nice to include the artwork in the insert. what i received was nothing short of an epic.

chocoa's workrate was like nothing i'd seen. maybe a day or two after we first agreed to work on this project together, i'd already received a few pieces of artwork from a story he wanted to tell, and until around May or June he drew another piece of artwork every single day. it got to a point where i was waking up each morning excited to see the next installment of his story, and he told it brilliantly. of course, there was the occasional struggle with burnout, but the final product that was delivered is something indescribable to me. as such, i hope you all will enjoy looking through the GO UNTIL YOU ARE GONE artbook, which is included with the bandcamp download, and every vinyl purchase! it gets quite meta, and it's very honest and touching, so please give it a chance. i think chocoa has a beautiful mind.

this particular work spoke to me like nothing else. when i saw it come through, the chaos, the color, the style, the beauty, the evocative, emotional, gripping nature of the painting... it spoke to me like artwork should. it reflected the album's ideas to a perfect t. the moment the artwork came through i immediately told chocoa i'd be using this for the cover. initially, i thought maybe i'd use just this picture, cropped to be square, but over time i kind of wanted to add a bit more of myself into it, which we'll get more into a bit later.

as the album began to come together, chocoa requested we add 2013.04 to the title, as this was to him, a moment in his life where things changed significantly. i loved the idea, as coincidentally i'd also been through a monumental paradigm shift in the year 2013, just 3 months later. july 2013 was when i moved to england, which massively altered the trajectory of my life. as such, '2013.04-07' became a welcome addition to the album title stylization.

the cover also has my handwriting in the topright corner, i just wanted it to be mine so it felt more personal! then there's the more violent imagery pasted on top. i've always been a fan of collage works, and the juxtaposition yet harmonious, uh, vibe(?) of having such 'extreme' imagery on top of a beautiful-yet-equally-sense-assaulting painting behind it felt very right to me. what's featured? well, let's take a closer look.

let's see, we've got an M1911A1 in *my* right hand (yes, those are my hands!), two stuck-together slices of mouldy, bloody bread, on dusty ground, with a broken, dilapidated CRT-television in the background, and further behind is a big factory in the midst of a grassy field. the hands have on bright white gloves that are, like the bread, bloodstained, and one glove has a seven-pointed star on it. i'll be honest, there's a lot of symbolism baked into this imagery, and i could share it with you all but in some ways i feel it speaks for itself, on its own. so, having described the image in detail, i'm going to leave it at that, and let your imaginations run wild! it's no fun if i spell out everything!!
the CRT is mine, but it wasn't always. actually, my GF and i happened upon it while on a walk, in march. here's a photo from when we first found it:
58bedd08-5602-440c-9d99-4fba64fffd14.jpg

well, damn! what a lucky find! i remember walking along the path and suddenly i saw something very artifical inside a long-torn-down brick building. i ventured into the overgrowth and snapped some pics of the TV. at the time, i really, really wanted to take it home because i thought it looked so cool, but we didn't have anything to carry it with and it was as heavy as the bricks that surrounded it, so we decided to leave it. but then an idea came to me, much like the title, of what this TV could represent in imagery, and i became obsessed with the concepts it held, so we went back for it a month later, and sure enough it was still sat there, covered in moss, dirt and birdshit.
8082c6dc-8f12-4fde-b52a-abdba8a7226d.jpg

here's a couple pics of me finding it once more and subsequently taking it home. something about seeing natural plantlife growing inside of something so artificial is wonderful. there's a sharpie on the table. initially i was planning on writing “THE CIRCUS” on the screen, or maybe on the shell somewhere, but i thought it was more striking standing alone, as itself. we didn't end up taking the cover photo until a couple months later. i had to wait for the bread to get mouldy, and i had to wait for a friend of mine to finish drawing the star on the white glove.
6e2fb9ab-8972-4adb-bd1f-7d7262988e03.jpg
here's a photo from the day, us walking through the woods nearby the field the photo was taken, carrying all the props and such we'd need.

this was by far the biggest effort i'd ever put into an album cover. it's not that i hadn't tried in the past, it was moreso i wanted to try *really hard* this time. i wanted to put my all into this project... i guess i always want to, but this felt special. why?

i'd been followed on instagram by a label back in early 2025. they focused on vaporwave, plunderphonics, barber beats etc. but said they were always looking for new artists, so i shot them an email and to my surprise they got back to me near immediately, asking for details about a project i wanted to put out. i happily sent them a wall of text as well as some demos from the album i'd cooked up to that point, and was shocked to receive an email saying they'd love to work with me. the moment i was told my album was going to get a vinyl press, i remember jumping out of bed after reading the email in the morning and punching the air a bunch (some kind of stim i do when i'm extremely happy, i guess). i was elated! and i knew i wanted the album to be perfectly suited to vinyl, in the way that old pink floyd or general prog-records were. i wanted to tell a story. now, this is a mantra i tend to follow across all albums i make (save for compilations, like SFI), but for this album in particular i knew the flow from the start of side a to the end of side b had to read as if you'd gone through another life entirely. when you listen to the album on vinyl, you can hear that the end of track 6 flows into the beginning of track 7 (don't you fucking dare say it) - which is where the record flips. like one is entering a cocoon, hiding away. i'll talk more about this in the part-two blog i'll inevitably have to post, because when these blogs get too full, the editor i use to write them tends to get a bit laggy.
needless to say, the entire album was planned carefully, and with the entirety of my love and dedication in mind at all times. i certainly went until i was... uh... went? LOL

now, the initial plan was to release the album in September. as such, i wanted all the tracks done by mid-June, but just before i had finished my first 'final pass', i was told the production would have to be delayed, and the order for the records couldn't be placed until September. i could've released the album in September regardless, but i knew i wanted the vinyl to launch alongside the record, so i in-turn decided to delay the release. and i'm very glad i did! the album finished production towards the beginning of September and i had gotten to a point where i was pleased (as one can be) with each track individually, as well as the overall flow of the album. then, something happened. i was stoned as fuck and suddenly got a message from the label saying they would no longer press my album.

i remember just dropping my phone and shutting down. i curled up on the couch. i felt like my life was over (okay, yes, i can be a bit dramatic, but this meant the world to me. i was also, as i mentioned, very stoned... so it was hard to rationalize any feelings in that moment). i was told the guy who ran the label was going to reach out to a friend of his about getting it pressed on their label instead, but to me, the album was as good as gone (pardon the pun). i reached out to some other labels amidst the wake but heard nothing. thankfully, connections sometimes pan out very well, and i ended up hearing back from the first label's friend. after some brief chats and detailing, we agreed the album would be released in the new year, pressed to beautiful blue vinyl. to be honest, until the album was physically in my hands, all i could think of was how terrified i was that it would all fall apart again. of course, that's nothing to do with Doki Doki Beats, it's moreso the fear i had gleaned from my interactions with the label before DDB.

so, the album wasn't a November release anymore, and the vinyl ended up being ordered on Halloween. one more delay was nothing, really. one crisp December morning, i woke up to some images of the vinyl, as well as a couple videos of it being played on a turntable, all courtesy of DDB. i'd never been more excited. my personal copy was shipped out thereafter, and arrived on the 23rd, a couple days before Christmas. the timing was perfect!
ace9b4bd-c6ed-4dd6-945e-1c8bf1a32167.jpg

with the vinyl in-hand, and release around the corner, all i could do was wait and hope. christmas was a nice distraction, and i had a friend visiting across the period so i tried to take my mind off the anticipation, but eventually release day came! and here we are, one week later!

that's the GO UNTIL YOU ARE GONE journey, really. now, for those who may be interested, in the next blog i'll talk more about the music itself, and how the symbolism and thematics seen here reflect sonically across the project. see you there!
